newsitem.title: GREECE: Greenpeace activists removed from Greek refinery.
newsitem.headline: Greenpeace activists removed from Greek refinery.

text.p: Coastguard special forces overran Greenpeace activists blockading Motor Oil, Greece's biggest oil refinery, on Wednesday and arrested 14 of them, Greenpeace said.

"Scores of special forces men carrying machine guns and knives removed activists chained around the facility. Our camera operator was injured during the attack," Greenpeace activist Stelios Psomas told Reuters.

Greenpeace blockaded the refinery's port facilities near the Corinth canal on Tuesday, accusing the firm, which is jointly owned by Saudi Aramco and the Vardiniyannis group, of polluting the environment.
Protesters chained themselves to mooring buoys and loading cranes while the Greekpeace ship Arctic Sunrise blocked access to the refinery's port. Greenpeace said the ship was still in place.
Motor Oil officials rejected accusations of a poor environmental record and demanded the removal of the demonstrators, saying they put the refinery's safety at risk.
